title.value: On Overfitting and Asymptotic Bias in Batch Reinforcement Learning with Partial Observability
title.justification: The title explicitly captures the core focus of the paper, which deals with overfitting and asymptotic bias in the context of batch reinforcement learning in partial observability scenarios.
title.quote: * This paper is an extended abstract of an article in the Journal of AI Research [François-Lavet et al., 2019].

analysis.description: This paper analyzes the tradeoff between overfitting and asymptotic bias in batch reinforcement learning with partial observability, providing theoretical insights and empirical illustrations on synthetic POMDPs.

type.justification: The paper provides a theoretical analysis of the tradeoff between overfitting and asymptotic bias, focusing on the formal characterization of state representation and the introduction of ϵ-sufficient statistics.
type.quote: In the context of reinforcement learning with partial observability, this paper provides an analysis of the tradeoff between these two sources of error. In particular, our theoretical analysis formally characterizes how a smaller state representation increases the asymptotic bias while decreasing the risk of overfitting.

name.justification: The paper deals primarily with the reinforcement learning setting, specifically in scenarios with partial observability and batch learning conditions.
name.quote: When an agent has limited information on its environment, the suboptimality of an RL algorithm can be decomposed into the sum of two terms: a term related to an asymptotic bias and a term due to overfitting.

name.justification: The paper focuses on reinforcement learning in the context of partial observability, and introduces concepts like POMDP, belief state, and history processing, which are central to the study of partially observable environments.
name.quote: In this paper, the conditional transition probabilities T , the reward function R and the conditional observation probabilities O are unknown. The only information available to the agent is the past experience it gathered while interacting with the POMDP.

name.justification: The paper examines scenarios where reinforcement learning is conducted with a fixed set of transition samples, without the possibility of acquiring new observations, which is a key characteristic of batch reinforcement learning.
name.quote: However, such E/E strategies are not applicable when the acquisition of new observations is not possible anymore. In the pure “batch” setting, the task is to learn the best possible policy from a fixed set of transition samples.

name.justification: The paper uses a distribution of synthetic POMDPs to empirically illustrate the theoretical results regarding the bias-overfitting tradeoff.
name.quote: Experiments on a POMDP with real-world data are available in the full paper.
